text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.31% today, a modest move that fits within a much stronger two-week rally of 7.81%. The gains appear tied to elevated oil and refined product prices: crude hit a six-week high after renewed Iran-U.S. military confrontation, gasoline prices topped $4 per gallon for Labor Day weekend (a record), and U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude oil prices and tight refinery utilization typically boost margins—the difference between what they pay for oil and what they earn selling gasoline and diesel.

The broader backdrop remains supportive: geopolitical tensions are keeping oil prices elevated, storage levels for both crude and gasoline remain relatively low, and refinery utilization is near maximum, all of which historically favor refiner profitability when demand is strong.
